summary: Reviewed orchestrator/tests/test_slug_dir.py (test-only WP, no production code changed).

TestLedgerLogCopyPath is well-structured: three sections separated by clear comments — deep paths (3 parametrized cases), shallow paths (3 parametrized cases), and full path shape (3 explicit tests). Module docstring updated to reference the new class.

_derive_ledger_log_dir() correctly mirrors cli.py lines 869-876 with a clear docstring explaining its test-isolation purpose and the future refactoring path. All parametrized inputs cover meaningful edge cases.
Test isolation is excellent: no file I/O, no CLI imports, pure pathlib operations. Tests are fast and deterministic.

The test-mirror pattern is a known limitation (if cli.py changes, both the mirror and production code drift silently). This is documented in the helper's docstring and accepted as the best achievable coverage without refactoring cli.py.
All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met. 18/18 tests pass.

comments.note: No behavioral issues found. The implementation is clean and well-structured. All AC confirmed met.

_derive_ledger_log_dir() is a necessary test-local mirror of inline production code in cli.py lines 869-876. This is the correct approach given that the production code is not yet extracted into a testable unit. The helper's docstring explicitly identifies its relationship to the production code and the refactoring path. The risk is that if cli.py's inline logic changes, both the helper and the production code will drift without a test failure to alert maintainers. This is a known limitation documented by the Developer, and WP-003's tests are the best coverage achievable without refactoring cli.py.

[documentation-forward] The _derive_ledger_log_dir() helper has a good docstring but does not include a reference to the WP or a TODO marker indicating this should be deleted once cli.py is refactored to expose a named function. Adding a # TODO: replace with call to production function once cli.py extracts ledger_log_dir derivation note would help future maintainers track this cleanup obligation.
